speciesGuide.rangesDesc: Petvity compares every logged metric against these species-specific baselines and flags anything outside the normal range automatically.
speciesGuide.physHeartRateDesc: Resting heart rate in beats per minute
speciesGuide.emotionalDesc: Beyond physical vitals, Petvity tracks four emotional dimensions that form your pet’s Digital Twin — a living portrait of how they’re really feeling.
speciesGuide.emotEnergyDesc: How active and lively your pet feels. Low energy can signal illness or pain.
speciesGuide.emotMoodDesc: Overall happiness and contentment. Tracks emotional wellbeing over time.
speciesGuide.emotAnxietyDesc: Calm vs. stressed. High anxiety is a key indicator of unmet needs or fear.
speciesGuide.emotSocializationDesc: Engagement with people and other animals. Withdrawal can be an early health signal.
speciesGuide.breedsDesc: Start with a breed from the list below or select “Mixed / Other” — the health ranges automatically adjust to your {species}’s species.
speciesGuide.tipsDesc: What to watch for when tracking your {species}’s health.
speciesGuide.dogBlurb: Dogs are highly expressive animals whose mood, energy, and body condition change visibly day to day. Consistent tracking lets you catch weight loss, lethargy, or anxiety before a vet visit is urgent.
speciesGuide.catBlurb: Cats are experts at hiding discomfort. Subtle changes in activity level, appetite, and social behaviour are often the first signs of illness. Daily logging surfaces patterns that are easy to miss.
speciesGuide.horseBlurb: Horses require careful monitoring of temperature, heart rate, and weight — small deviations can indicate colic, laminitis, or infection. Petvity makes it easy to spot trends before they become emergencies.
speciesGuide.dogTip1: Weigh monthly — weight change > 10% warrants a vet check
speciesGuide.dogTip2: Normal temperature: 38.0–39.0 °C (rectal). Anything above 39.5 °C is fever.
speciesGuide.dogTip3: Heart rate varies by size: small breeds 100–140 bpm, large breeds 60–100 bpm
speciesGuide.dogTip4: Energy dips lasting > 2 days are worth logging and watching closely
speciesGuide.dogTip5: Track mood after major changes (new pet, house move, routine shift)
speciesGuide.catTip1: Cats are obligate carnivores — even mild weight loss can indicate illness
speciesGuide.catTip2: Normal temperature: 38.0–39.25 °C. Cats run slightly higher than dogs.
speciesGuide.catTip3: Heart rate at rest: 120–220 bpm — a wide range, consistent baseline matters
speciesGuide.catTip4: A sudden drop in socialization score is a key early-warning signal in cats
speciesGuide.catTip5: Anxiety spikes correlate with litter box issues, hiding, or over-grooming
speciesGuide.horseTip1: Weigh weekly with a weight tape — horses fluctuate with season and workload
speciesGuide.horseTip2: Normal temperature: 37.5–38.5 °C. Fever above 38.5 °C warrants investigation.
speciesGuide.horseTip3: Resting heart rate 28–44 bpm. Above 50 at rest is a veterinary concern.
speciesGuide.horseTip4: Daily gut sounds and manure output are as important as temperature
speciesGuide.horseTip5: Anxiety tracking helps identify tack fit problems, social stress, or pain
speciesGuide.birdBlurb: Birds are sensitive to environmental changes and routine disruptions. Weight loss, feather quality shifts, and behavioral changes are often the first visible signs of illness — daily observation is essential.
speciesGuide.birdTip1: Weigh weekly — birds hide illness instinctively; a drop > 10% needs prompt vet attention
speciesGuide.birdTip2: Monitor droppings daily — changes in color, consistency, or quantity signal health problems
speciesGuide.birdTip3: Track vocalization patterns — an unusually quiet bird is often a sick bird
speciesGuide.birdTip4: Energy dips lasting > 2 days alongside reduced appetite are early warning signs
speciesGuide.birdTip5: Socialization drops in flock birds (parrots, cockatiels) frequently precede illness
speciesGuide.rabbitBlurb: Rabbits instinctively conceal pain and illness. GI stasis, dental disease, and respiratory infections are common — daily tracking of weight, intake, and behavior catches problems before they become emergencies.
speciesGuide.rabbitTip1: Weigh weekly — rabbits lose condition quickly; > 5% loss in a week warrants vet attention
speciesGuide.rabbitTip2: Monitor gut sounds — silence for > 1 hour combined with reduced food intake indicates GI stasis, a veterinary emergency
speciesGuide.rabbitTip3: Heart rate 130–325 bpm; elevated rate combined with hunched posture signals pain
speciesGuide.rabbitTip4: Track cecotrope consumption — skipping them is an early sign of dental or GI problems
speciesGuide.rabbitTip5: Socialization drops combined with tooth grinding or hunched posture = pain; seek vet care
speciesGuide.guineaPigBlurb: Guinea pigs are social, vocal animals whose condition can deteriorate rapidly when ill. Consistent weight monitoring and attention to eating habits are the most important daily health habits.
speciesGuide.guineaPigTip1: Weigh weekly — guinea pigs mask illness; a drop > 50 g in one week warrants attention
speciesGuide.guineaPigTip2: Normal temperature: 37.2–39.5 °C. Heatstroke risk rises sharply above 26 °C ambient
speciesGuide.guineaPigTip3: Heart rate 230–380 bpm; labored breathing or panting needs immediate veterinary attention
speciesGuide.guineaPigTip4: Track vocalization — a quiet guinea pig is often an unwell guinea pig
speciesGuide.guineaPigTip5: Vitamin C deficiency (scurvy) is common; monitor daily food intake and mobility closely
speciesGuide.hamsterBlurb: Hamsters age rapidly — health changes that take weeks in dogs can unfold in days. Daily observation of weight, coat, and behavior is critical given their short lifespan.
speciesGuide.hamsterTip1: Weigh every 2–3 days — a 10% weight drop is equivalent to severe illness and requires same-day vet care
speciesGuide.hamsterTip2: Watch for wet tail (profuse watery diarrhea) — a veterinary emergency requiring treatment within hours
speciesGuide.hamsterTip3: Wheel usage is a reliable energy proxy — sudden drop in nightly running is an early warning sign
speciesGuide.hamsterTip4: Track coat condition — rough, dull fur combined with weight loss signals systemic illness
speciesGuide.hamsterTip5: Distinguish torpor from death: if unresponsive, warm gently — torpor at cool temperatures can mimic death
speciesGuide.reptileBlurb: Reptiles are ectothermic and highly sensitive to temperature, humidity, and UVB lighting. Most health problems stem from husbandry errors — consistent environment checks alongside health metrics prevent the majority of issues.
speciesGuide.reptileTip1: Ensure a proper thermal gradient — most species need a basking spot of 30–35 °C and a cool side of 22–26 °C
speciesGuide.reptileTip2: Weigh monthly — weight loss > 10% over four weeks warrants a fecal exam for parasites
speciesGuide.reptileTip3: Track shedding cycles — retained shed or incomplete ecdysis signals humidity or nutritional problems
speciesGuide.reptileTip4: Monitor feeding response on schedule — appetite changes are the clearest early illness signal in reptiles
speciesGuide.reptileTip5: Lethargy beyond normal brumation patterns, or combined with discoloration, warrants veterinary attention
speciesGuide.fishBlurb: Fish health is directly tied to water quality. Most disease is preventable through consistent monitoring of water parameters alongside daily behavioral and physical observation.
speciesGuide.fishTip1: Observe daily — clamped fins, labored breathing, or surface gasping require immediate action
speciesGuide.fishTip2: Track feeding response — reduced appetite is often the first sign of illness or deteriorating water quality
speciesGuide.fishTip3: Temperature stability matters as much as the exact value — rapid fluctuations stress immune function
speciesGuide.fishTip4: Behavioral changes (hiding, flashing against objects, isolation) typically precede visible symptoms
speciesGuide.fishTip5: Weigh if possible; otherwise use body condition scoring — a hollow belly or pinecone-like scales signal serious illness
speciesGuide.ctaDesc: Free forever. Log daily health data, get automatic wellness signals, and build a complete health record you can share with your vet.

home.metaTitle: {app} — The global platform for pet care
home.metaDesc: Track your pet's health signals, connect with vets and sitters, shop essentials, and manage adoption — all in one place. Free forever.
home.heroSubtitle: One daily check-in builds a living Digital Twin of your pet. When something shifts, {app} tells you what — and puts everything you need next in one place: trusted vets, sitters and groomers, a marketplace, and a humane adoption network.
home.featuresDesc: From daily check-ins to full medical histories — everything your vet wishes you kept track of.
home.trackingTitle: Know what's normal. Catch what isn't.
home.trackingBody: Log weight, temperature, heart rate, energy, and mood in under a minute. Petvity compares every entry against species-specific normal ranges — automatically flagging anything worth watching.
home.recordsTitle: Everything your vet wishes you tracked.
home.recordsBody: Vet visits, vaccinations, medications, lab results, surgeries — all in one place, always at your fingertips. Bring a complete history to every appointment instead of relying on memory.
home.twinP1: Vitals tell you what. The Digital Twin tells you how. It combines mood, energy, anxiety, and socialization into a single living portrait — updated every time you log a check-in.
home.twinP2: Four emotional states — Thriving, Doing Well, Needs Attention, or Struggling — plus a trend indicator so you can see whether things are improving or declining before they become a problem.
home.signalsP: Every day, Petvity compares your pet's metrics against species-specific normal ranges. Three states. No guesswork. One clear signal.
home.signalHealthyDesc: All metrics in range. Vaccinations current. Keep doing what you're doing.
home.signalWatchDesc: One metric slightly outside normal range, or a booster coming due soon.
home.signalConcernDesc: Multiple out-of-range readings, or an overdue vaccination. Book a vet visit.
home.ecosystemDesc: Health tracking is just the start. Petvity is the only platform that covers the complete care journey — from daily check-ins to finding a vet to giving a pet a home.
home.vetTitle: Find a Vet, Sitter or Groomer
home.vetDesc: Search trusted veterinarians, sitters, and groomers near you. See real reviews and availability, and book directly — without leaving the platform.
home.mktDesc: Shop food, supplements, toys, and accessories — all in the same app you use to track health. No switching between sites.
home.adoptDesc: List a pet for adoption or find your next companion. Full application workflow, cross-border listings, and direct messaging between owners.
home.howDesc: No training. No setup fee. Just sign up and start.
home.step2Desc: Name, species, breed, birthdate, photo. Dogs, cats, horses, and more.
home.step3Desc: Record vitals and mood. The wellness signal and Digital Twin update instantly.
home.pricingDesc: Every feature — health tracking, digital twin, vet network, marketplace, and adoption listings — is included free with no pet limits.
home.pricingF5: Find & book vets and pet sitters
home.finalDesc: Free forever. No credit card. Add your first pet in under a minute — and see your Digital Twin on your first check-in.
home.liveProofTitle: Real pets, tracked in the open
home.liveProofDesc: Milo and Rosie live on Petvity. Their check-ins are logged every day and their profiles are public — no screenshots, no staging. Open one and watch a real health history grow.

pricing.faq1Q: Is the Free plan really free forever?
pricing.faq1A: Yes. The Free plan is designed to be the permanent home for individual pet owners. We'll never move core health-tracking features behind a paywall.
pricing.faq2Q: How many pets can I add?
pricing.faq2A: Unlimited. Whether you have one dog or a stable of horses, the Free plan handles it all.
pricing.faq3A: Dogs, cats, horses, birds, rabbits, guinea pigs, hamsters, reptiles, fish, and more via the 'Other' category. Each species has its own normal ranges for health metrics.
pricing.faq4Q: When will Pro and Clinic plans launch?
pricing.faq4A: The core platform is live and free. Pro and Clinic tiers for breeders and veterinary businesses are next. Join the waitlist to be notified.
pricing.faq5Q: Can I use {app} in my language?
pricing.faq5A: {app} supports English, German, French, Spanish, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Turkish, and Arabic (with full right-to-left layout).
pricing.faq6A: All data is owner-scoped — you can only see your own pets. We use encrypted connections, bcrypt password hashing, and host on our own self-hosted European infrastructure.

about.metaDesc: {app} is the global platform for pet care — helping owners track wellness, connect with vets, and give their pets the life they deserve.
about.heroP1: {app} was born from a frustrating pattern: noticing something was off with a pet, not being able to articulate exactly what, and arriving at the vet with a vague "he just seems a bit off." We wanted data. So we built it.
about.heroP2: Then we kept going — because good data is only half the job. You also need a vet who can interpret it, products your pet actually needs, and a network that can find every animal a home. That's {app}.
about.missionTitle: Turn a pet owner's instinct into a signal a vet can act on
about.missionP1: Every pet owner has an intuition about their animal. Something's different. Quieter than usual. Eating a bit less. Sleeping more. These signals matter — but without data, they're impossible to communicate with precision, and easy to dismiss.
about.missionP2: Petvity turns those observations into a structured health record and a living Digital Twin. When you arrive at the vet saying "her energy score dropped from 4 to 2 over the last eight days and her Digital Twin shifted from Thriving to Needs Attention," that's a workable clinical picture — not a vague feeling.
about.missionP3: But data alone isn't enough. We also connect owners to the vets and sitters who can respond, the products their pets need, and a global adoption network — because the full care journey happens on one platform, not five.
about.valuesTitle: How we think about building this
about.v1Desc: Vets can only see what happens in the clinic. What happens at home — the subtle changes in energy, the skipped meal, the restless night — is invisible to everyone. Petvity makes that data visible and actionable.
about.v2Desc: Pets don't respect borders. Neither does our platform. Petvity supports 9 languages — including full right-to-left Arabic — because a pet owner in Tokyo or Istanbul deserves the same tools as one in San Francisco.
about.v3Desc: We don't sell your data, share it with advertisers, or use it to train AI models without consent. Owner-scoped queries mean you can only ever see your own pets.
about.v4Desc: Knowing your pet's signal is valuable. But the platform doesn't stop there — it connects you directly to vets who can act on it, products your pet needs, and a network that can find every animal a home.
about.longP1: Most pet apps do one thing. Petvity connects the whole picture: daily health data feeds a Digital Twin, the twin surfaces a wellness signal, the signal tells you whether to book a vet — and the vet is two taps away. That closed loop is what makes it useful every day, not just when something goes wrong.
about.longP2: We also build VitaReBa — a clinic management portal for rehabilitation therapists — and are exploring how shared health data infrastructure can power better care decisions across the human–animal spectrum. Long-term: IoT sensors and cameras feeding real-time physiological data directly into each pet's Digital Twin.
